title: Finish fallible steps before the irreversible effect

facts.note: Role (PLT-84), mapped to paths by the structure profile.
Observer: a use case performs a side effect and other work in the same request.
Diff places a call that can fail (configuration lookup, pricing, validation, I/O) after a write.

fires: A use case debits a balance and only then looks up configuration that can throw.
A record of the effect is written in a second step that can fail.
doesNotFire: Operations whose single write is the last step.

given: A use case performs an effect that cannot be undone silently and also runs steps that can fail
then: Run every step that can fail before the effect, or record a compensation that runs when a later step fails.
prefer: Compute the full outcome, validate and load configuration first, then perform the effect and its record together.
If that sequence is impossible, make the compensation explicit and test it.
avoid: Effect first, then lookups that may throw.
Writing the effect and its record in separate, independently failing steps.
why: A failure after the effect leaves state changed with no record or response, which is the hardest inconsistency to detect and repair.
evidence: A test forces a later step to fail and observes no effect, or a completed compensation.
